newsitem.title: USA: House votes for 'partial birth' abortion ban.
newsitem.headline: House votes for 'partial birth' abortion ban.

text.p: A controversial ban on so-called "partial birth" abortion was approved by the House of Representatives by a wide, apparently veto-proof margin on Thursday.

Members of the House voted 295-136 for the ban, which allows exceptions in cases where the pregnant woman's life is at risk. President Clinton, who has insisted on another exception for when a woman's health is in jeopardy, has vowed to veto the bill. A vote of 290 or more is needed to override the veto, as well as a two-thirds majority in the Senate.

Clinton vetoed an identical bill last year, and the White House said in a statement issued on Wednesday that the new bill contained "the same serious flaws" as last year's and Clinton would veto it for the same reasons.

"By refusing to permit women, in reliance on their doctors' best medical judgment, to use this procedure when their lives are threatened or when their health is put in serious jeopardy, the Congress has fashioned a bill that is consistent neither with the Constitution nor with sound public policy," Clinton said in his 1996 veto message.
The procedure involves the partial extraction of the foetus feet-first, the subsequent suctioning out of the foetal brain and removal of the foetus.
Opponents of the ban have said it hampers women's constitutional rights to choose abortion. Proponents of the ban call the procedure barbaric.
